name: application-checkout-order-summary
title: Checkout Order Summary
description: Itemized subtotal, shipping, and tax with an applicable promo code field and a computed total, ending in a checkout action.
useWhen: Building a cart or checkout page that needs a running breakdown of costs before purchase.
You want to let users apply a promo/discount code and see it reflected in the total immediately.
Pairing with `cart-line-item` rows to build a full cart-to-checkout flow.
avoidWhen: You only need to show a single final price with no breakdown — a plain price display is simpler than a full summary.
The purchase flow has no shipping or tax concepts (e.g. digital-only, single fixed price) — drop those rows rather than showing $0.00 placeholders.
You need multi-currency or tax-jurisdiction logic — this pattern renders whatever numbers you compute; it does not calculate tax or shipping itself.
responsiveBehavior: Single-column card that stacks below cart line items on narrow viewports and sits in a fixed-width side rail on wider checkout layouts.
accessibility: Cost rows use <dl>/<dt>/<dd> so the label-value relationship is conveyed semantically, not just visually via flex alignment.
The promo code field has an associated (visually hidden) label rather than relying on placeholder text alone.
The applied promo line communicates savings through visible text (a minus sign and the code), not color alone.
The total is visually the largest text in the summary, reflecting its priority in the information hierarchy.

variants.title: Checkout Order Summary
variants.description: Subtotal, shipping, tax, an applied promo code with its discount, computed total, and a checkout button.
accessibility: The total recalculates from real subtotal/shipping/tax/discount state rather than being a static hardcoded figure.

variants.title: Checkout Order Summary (Dark)
variants.description: Checkout order summary adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Discount text color is tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface while remaining visually distinct from neutral rows.
